claim: On macOS 27.0.1 (26A434) aned performs no client-conditional zeroing of the perf-stats mask inside loadModel: the client-supplied options[kANEFPerformanceStatsMaskKey] is extracted, run through +[ANEPerformanceStats driverMaskForANEFMask:] (@0x10001ced8, framework-side translation), installed via setPerfStatsMask:, and forwarded unmodified to the kernel handoff createProgramInstanceForModel:...statsMask: (fetch @0x10001f1ac, call @0x10001f290); the only userspace candidate for the third-party zero is therefore the driverMaskForANEFMask translation table or the kernel IOKit path (initStatsBufferSection), and the mask participates in the program cache key, so mask experiments recompile cached programs.
source: results/EXP-031-ane-perfstats-spy/raw/aned.text.asm.gz (otool -tV, arm64e slice) — walk documented in knowledge/ane/12-perfstats-and-entitlements.md Q3
evidence: extract-translate-install triple at 0x10001cecc/ced8/cee4 (repeat 0x10001e730, 0x100024860, 0x10002a004); no branch between entry and handoff; statsMask=%u log @0x10000385c prints forwarded value
caveat: which of framework-table vs kernel zeroes the mask is unresolved without an IOKit trace (needs sudo); the XPC-acceptance entitlement gate (@0x10000e4bc, presence+boolValue) is separate, soft, and never the blocker for us — our connections are accepted

claim: Ad-hoc re-signing cannot buy ANE perf-stats: on both M5 Max and M4 mini (26A434) asserting com.apple.ane.iokit-user-access or com.apple.ANECompilerService.allow on an ad-hoc binary gets it SIGKILLed by AMFI (rc=137, 'code signature validation failed fatally', kernel load error 4), only com.apple.security.* keys survive ad-hoc, and the surviving-key build's kANE probe is unchanged (stats buffer size=0, rc=138, coreAnalyticsClientType=ThirdPartyAppUsingANE, StatsMask=0) — the gate is bound to the Apple-issued signing identity (team ID ''), which ad-hoc signatures cannot forge.
source: results/EXP-031-ane-perfstats-spy/README.md §Method-4 + raw/kane-run-c5-signed-studio.txt + raw/kane-run-c5-signed-mini.txt ; AMFI/kernel log lines in raw/
evidence: key-by-key launch bisect: iokit-user-access rc=137, ANECompilerService.allow rc=137, disable-library-validation rc=0; security find-identity: 0 valid identities on box
caveat: the one untested escalation is a real (dev-team) certificate: whether a NON-Apple but non-empty team ID promotes the client class is unknown — both fleet boxes have zero codesigning identities; owner decision to provision one closes this in one command

claim: The adapter-weights entitlement check in aned is soft, configurable, and its 'No entitlement!' log line is diagnostic rather than fatal: loadModelNewInstance consults an ANEConfig-provided boot-arg bypass (adapterWeightsAccessEntitlementBypassBootArg + isBoolBootArgSetTrue:) and an ANEConfig-NAMED entitlement key (adapterWeightsAccessEntitlement) via valueForEntitlement:+boolValue (@0x100021134-0x100021204), and the 'No entitlement!' emitter at 0x1000228a0 sits on a log-enabled check (cbnz @0x100021644) with execution continuing at 0x10002164c — loads proceed regardless.
evidence: cbnz @0x100021644 gates only os_log type check; fallthrough continues @0x10002164c
caveat: practical relevance: third parties reading 'No entitlement!' in aned logs as a failure are misreading a debug line; the actual denial semantics for adapter weights live further down the kernel path we did not walk
